name: Printing Digits of an Integer from Right to Left
description: Construct a program that prints the digits of an integer from right to left.

comments.content: We need variable num to store the integer that we want to print its digits.
We need variable lastDigit to point to the digit in the 1's position of the integer.

We need to process the digits of the integer from right to left and print them. Therefore, we need to use a loop structure. In this program, we do this by using a do loop. The do loop is more appropriate than a while loop because a positive integer always has at least one digit which results in the body of the loop performing at least once.

We need to extract the last digit in the 1's position of the integer. For example, if the integer is 1234, we want to extract the digit 4 that is in 1's position of the integer. We do this by calculating the remainder of the division of the integer by 10.
This statement prints each digit in the integer to the default standard output stream. Each printed digit is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.

We truncate the extracted digit that we processed from the original integer by dividing the integer by 10. Note that this statement performs an integer division because both operand of the / operator are integer. Therefore, this division will remove the digit that we processed (lastDigit) and we can move on to the next digit.

We need to check for termination conditions to avoid infinite loops. The body of the while loop should repeat as long as there are more digits left that we have not processed yet. The loop should terminate when we run out of digits to process.

We could check whether the are more digits left by checking whether the variable num, which gets updated in the body of the do loop, is greater than zero. If variable num is greater than zero, then it must have at least one digit, and in that case, the body of the do loop will be repeated again.
